elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed..." — applies to each Party symmetrically.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cap is the sum of (a) SFJ's Development Costs and (b) PB's Article 6/Section 14.2 payments in the preceding 12 months; there is no "greater of" construction and no USD 1,000,000 floor.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 15.11: "NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, RELIANCE OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES..." — mutual on its face.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "Excluded Claims" expressly includes "breach of its confidentiality obligations", and the cap opens "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The Excluded Claims definition lists only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out was added.
"Excluded Claims" means "a Party's indemnification obligations...", carved out of the cap.
"gross negligence" is listed within the Excluded Claims definition.
"willful misconduct" is listed within the Excluded Claims definition.
Fraud does not appear in the Excluded Claims definition or elsewhere as an exception to the new cap.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out appears in the Excluded Claims definition; IP claims would fall inside the new aggregate cap.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: The only preserved language is the retained "FOR THE AVOIDANCE OF DOUBT, THIS SECTION 15.11 IS NOT MEANT TO LIMIT PB'S OBLIGATION TO PAY SFJ THE AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 6 OR SECTION 14.2" — a narrow named subset of PB payment streams, not PB's payment obligations as a whole; its interaction with the newly appended cap sentence is also positionally ambiguous.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed..." — no one-sided drafting; no residual language stating either Party's liability is unlimited.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: The Agreement has no "Fees" concept; the cap is pegged to determinate consideration streams — Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ (defined at 1.1.57, including the SFJ Interim/Final Management Fees) plus PB's Article 6 and Section 14.2 payments — "in each case during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim". The temporal anchor is 12 months and the measure is not illusory in either direction.
"Except for Excluded Claims..."; Excluded Claims includes "a Party's indemnification obligations".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims includes "breach of its confidentiality obligations".

reasons: Fallback level is complete: one inserted sentence supplies a mutual aggregate cap measured over the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct expressly carved out as Excluded Claims.

Preferred level fails on five elements: no "greater of" formulation and no USD 1,000,000 floor; no uncapped carve-out for data protection/security breaches, fraud, or infringement of the other Party's IP; and no general exclusion of PB's payment obligations from capped damages (the retained avoidance-of-doubt sentence reaches only Article 6 and Section 14.2 amounts). To reach preferred, amend the inserted sentence to "the greater of (a) [the 12-month payment measure] and (b) USD 1,000,000", extend Excluded Claims to "breach of its data protection or security obligations, ... fraud, and infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights", and add "PB's payment obligations under this Agreement are not subject to this cap".

Minimality holds: nothing was deleted, the favourable existing mutual consequential-damages waiver in 15.11 and the arbitration waiver in 15.10.2.4 are retained, and the insertion adds no survival tail, expense language, procedure or damages category beyond the four fallback carve-outs. The two-component measure is necessitated by the absence of any "Fees" concept in this Co-Development Agreement rather than being an unnecessary enlargement.

Intent is preserved: no undefined term is introduced (Development Costs is defined at 1.1.57; Article 6 and Section 14.2 are live cross-references) and the retained "for the avoidance of doubt" sentence harmonises with rather than contradicts the new cap. Recommend appending the new sentence expressly within Section 15.11 (or cross-referencing it) so the avoidance-of-doubt sentence unambiguously governs the new cap sentence as well.

Strategic note for the drafter: because PB's payment obligations under Article 6/14.2 are preserved outside the limitation while SFJ's Development Cost funding obligation is not similarly preserved, the new mutual cap bites asymmetrically against our client's recovery for an SFJ funding failure. Consider adding "a Party's obligation to pay amounts due under this Agreement (including SFJ's obligation to fund Development Costs)" to the Excluded Claims list — this also delivers the outstanding preferred payment-obligations element.
